sanskrit: yathā tāṃ buddhim āsthāya gatim agryāṃ gamiṣyasi śṛṇu dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha gadataḥ sarvam eva me
english: How, taking your stand upon that understanding, you shall attain the supreme goal — hear it all from me as I speak, O best of those who uphold the Law.

sanskrit: āgacchad brāhmaṇaḥ kaś cit svargalokād ariṃdama brahmalokāc ca durdharṣaḥ so 'smābhiḥ pūjito 'bhavat
english: A certain brāhmaṇa once came, O subduer of foes, from the world of heaven and from the world of Brahmā — one hard to assail — and by us he was duly honored.

sanskrit: asmābhiḥ paripṛṣṭaś ca yad āha bharatarṣabha divyena vidhinā pārtha tac chṛṇuṣvāvicārayan
english: And being questioned by us, what he declared, O bull of the Bharatas, by a divine method, O Pārtha — hear that with an undoubting mind.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca mokṣadharmaṃ samāśritya kṛṣṇa yan mānupṛcchasi bhūtānām anukampārthaṃ yan mohacchedanaṃ prabho
english: The brāhmaṇa said: That which you ask of me, O Kṛṣṇa, resting upon the Law of liberation — for the sake of compassion toward beings, that which cuts away delusion, O Lord —

sanskrit: tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yathāvan madhusūdana śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā gadato mama mādhava
english: that I shall fully declare to you just as it is, O slayer of Madhu; listen attentively as I speak, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: kaś cid vipras tapoyuktaḥ kāśyapo dharmavittamaḥ āsasāda dvijaṃ kaṃ cid dharmāṇām āgatāgamam
english: A certain learned brāhmaṇa, Kāśyapa, devoted to austerity and most versed in the Law, approached a certain twice-born who had mastered the traditions of dharma,

sanskrit: gatāgate subahuśo jñānavijñānapāragam lokatattvārthakuśalaṃ jñātāraṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
english: one who had come and gone many times, who had crossed to the far shore of knowledge and discernment, skilled in the truth and meaning of the worlds, a knower of pleasure and pain,

sanskrit: jātīmaraṇatattvajñaṃ kovidaṃ puṇyapāpayoḥ draṣṭāram uccanīcānāṃ karmabhir dehināṃ gatim
english: a knower of the truth of birth and death, expert in merit and demerit, a seer of the high and low destinies that embodied beings reach by their deeds,

sanskrit: carantaṃ muktavat siddhaṃ praśāntaṃ saṃyatendriyam dīpyamānaṃ śriyā brāhmyā kramamāṇaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: who wandered like one already liberated, a perfected one, serene, his senses restrained, blazing with the splendor of Brahman and moving everywhere at will,

sanskrit: antardhānagatijñaṃ ca śrutvā tattvena kāśyapaḥ tathaivāntarhitaiḥ siddhair yāntaṃ cakradharaiḥ saha
english: and one who knew the art of vanishing — so Kāśyapa truly learned — moving along with hidden perfected ones who bore the discus,

sanskrit: saṃbhāṣamāṇam ekānte samāsīnaṃ ca taiḥ saha yadṛcchayā ca gacchantam asaktaṃ pavanaṃ yathā
english: conversing with them apart and sitting together with them, and going wherever he wished, unattached like the wind.

sanskrit: taṃ samāsādya medhāvī sa tadā dvijasattamaḥ caraṇau dharmakāmo vai tapasvī susamāhitaḥ pratipede yathānyāyaṃ bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ
english: Approaching him, that wise and most excellent twice-born, an ascetic eager for the Law, well-composed, did him reverence at his feet as is proper, filled with the highest devotion.

sanskrit: vismitaś cādbhutaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāśyapas taṃ dvijottamam paricāreṇa mahatā guruṃ vaidyam atoṣayat
english: And amazed at seeing this marvel, Kāśyapa gratified that most excellent twice-born, his learned teacher, with great and attentive service.

sanskrit: prītātmā copapannaś ca śrutacāritrasaṃyutaḥ bhāvena toṣayac cainaṃ guruvṛttyā paraṃtapaḥ
english: With a glad heart, fit and endowed with learning and good conduct, that scorcher of foes pleased him sincerely with the service due to a teacher.

sanskrit: tasmai tuṣṭaḥ sa śiṣyāya prasanno 'thābravīd guruḥ siddhiṃ parām abhiprekṣya śṛṇu tan me janārdana
english: Pleased and gracious toward that pupil, the teacher then spoke, looking to the highest perfection — hear it from me, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: vividhaiḥ karmabhis tāta puṇyayogaiś ca kevalaiḥ gacchantīha gatiṃ martyā devaloke 'pi ca sthitim
english: By manifold deeds, my son, and by purely meritorious practices, mortals reach their destiny here and a dwelling even in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: na kva cit sukham atyantaṃ na kva cic chāśvatī sthitiḥ sthānāc ca mahato bhraṃśo duḥkhalabdhāt punaḥ punaḥ
english: Nowhere is there utter happiness, nowhere an everlasting station; and there is a fall, again and again, from a high place won with pain.

sanskrit: aśubhā gatayaḥ prāptāḥ kaṣṭā me pāpasevanāt kāmamanyuparītena tṛṣṇayā mohitena ca
english: Evil and grievous destinies have I reached through the pursuit of sin, overcome by desire and wrath and deluded by craving.

sanskrit: punaḥ punaś ca maraṇaṃ janma caiva punaḥ punaḥ āhārā vividhā bhuktāḥ pītā nānāvidhāḥ stanāḥ
english: Again and again death, and birth again and again; manifold foods have I eaten, and many kinds of breasts have I suckled.

sanskrit: mātaro vividhā dṛṣṭāḥ pitaraś ca pṛthagvidhāḥ sukhāni ca vicitrāṇi duḥkhāni ca mayānagha
english: Manifold mothers have I seen, and fathers of many kinds, and varied joys and sorrows, O sinless one.

sanskrit: priyair vivāso bahuśaḥ saṃvāsaś cāpriyaiḥ saha dhananāśaś ca saṃprāpto labdhvā duḥkhena tad dhanam
english: Often parting from those I loved and dwelling together with those I disliked; and loss of wealth came upon me after I had won that wealth with pain.

sanskrit: avamānāḥ sukaṣṭāś ca parataḥ svajanāt tathā śārīrā mānasāś cāpi vedanā bhṛśadāruṇāḥ
english: And grievous humiliations, from strangers and likewise from my own kin, and agonies of body and mind, exceedingly cruel.

sanskrit: prāptā vimānanāś cogrā vadhabandhāś ca dāruṇāḥ patanaṃ niraye caiva yātanāś ca yamakṣaye
english: Fierce indignities have come upon me, and terrible slayings and bondages, and a fall into hell, and torments in the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: jarā rogāś ca satataṃ vāsanāni ca bhūriśaḥ loke 'sminn anubhūtāni dvaṃdvajāni bhṛśaṃ mayā
english: Old age and diseases without end, and lingering distresses in abundance, born of the pairs of opposites, have all been keenly suffered by me in this world.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cin nirvedān nikārān nikṛtena ca lokatantraṃ parityaktaṃ duḥkhārtena bhṛśaṃ mayā tataḥ siddhir iyaṃ prāptā prasādād ātmano mayā
english: Then at last, out of revulsion, out of humiliations and treacheries, the whole machinery of worldly life was wholly abandoned by me, sorely afflicted; and so this perfection was attained by me through the grace of my own self.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ punar ihāgantā lokān ālokayāmy aham ā siddher ā prajāsargād ātmano me gatiḥ śubhā
english: No more shall I come hither; I look upon the worlds from above. Up to perfection, up to the creation of beings, blessed is the course of my self.

sanskrit: upalabdhā dvijaśreṣṭha tatheyaṃ siddhir uttamā itaḥ paraṃ gamiṣyāmi tataḥ parataraṃ punaḥ brahmaṇaḥ padam avyagraṃ mā te bhūd atra saṃśayaḥ
english: This highest perfection has been won, O best of the twice-born; from here I shall go beyond, and beyond that again to the untroubled station of Brahman — let there be no doubt of this in you.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ punar ihāgantā martyalokaṃ paraṃtapa prīto 'smi te mahāprājña brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: No more shall I come again to the world of mortals, O scorcher of foes. I am pleased with you, O greatly wise one; say what I may do for you.

sanskrit: yadīpsur upapannas tvaṃ tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ abhijāne ca tad ahaṃ yadarthaṃ mā tvam āgataḥ acirāt tu gamiṣyāmi yenāhaṃ tvām acūcudam
english: For whatever you have come seeking, the time for it has now arrived; and I know full well the purpose for which you have come to me. But soon I shall depart, by that path toward which I have urged you.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ prīto 'smi bhavataś cāritreṇa vicakṣaṇa paripṛccha yāvad bhavate bhāṣeyaṃ yat tavepsitam
english: Greatly am I pleased with your conduct, O discerning one; ask, while I may speak to you whatever you desire.

sanskrit: bahu manye ca te buddhiṃ bhṛśaṃ saṃpūjayāmi ca yenāhaṃ bhavatā buddho medhāvī hy asi kāśyapa
english: I esteem your understanding highly and honor it greatly, for by you I have been rightly understood; for you are wise, O Kāśyapa.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tatas tasyopasaṃgṛhya pādau praśnān sudurvacān papraccha tāṃś ca sarvān sa prāha dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Then, clasping his feet, he asked questions exceedingly hard to answer; and that best of upholders of the Law declared them all.

sanskrit: kāśyapa uvāca kathaṃ śarīraṃ cyavate kathaṃ caivopapadyate kathaṃ kaṣṭāc ca saṃsārāt saṃsaran parimucyate
english: Kāśyapa said: How does the body fall away, and how does it come into being? And how, wandering through grievous transmigration, is one set free?

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ vā kathaṃ yuktvā tac charīraṃ vimuñcati śarīrataś ca nirmuktaḥ katham anyat prapadyate
english: And how, having yoked the self, does it release that body? And freed from the body, how does it pass on to another?

sanskrit: kathaṃ śubhāśubhe cāyaṃ karmaṇī svakṛte naraḥ upabhuṅkte kva vā karma videhasyopatiṣṭhati
english: And how does this man enjoy the fruits of the good and evil deeds he himself has done? And where does the deed abide for one who is without a body?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca evaṃ saṃcoditaḥ siddhaḥ praśnāṃs tān pratyabhāṣata ānupūrvyeṇa vārṣṇeya yathā tan me vacaḥ śṛṇu
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Thus prompted, the perfected one answered those questions in due order, O Vārṣṇeya; hear that word of mine as it was.

sanskrit: siddha uvāca āyuḥkīrtikarāṇīha yāni karmāṇi sevate śarīragrahaṇe 'nyasmiṃs teṣu kṣīṇeṣu sarvaśaḥ
english: The perfected one said: Those deeds that promote life and renown, which one performs here at the taking of a particular body — when these are wholly exhausted,

sanskrit: āyuḥkṣayaparītātmā viparītāni sevate buddhir vyāvartate cāsya vināśe pratyupasthite
english: his self beset by the wasting of life, he engages in things contrary to his good, and his understanding turns awry as destruction draws near.

sanskrit: sattvaṃ balaṃ ca kālaṃ cāpy aviditvātmanas tathā ativelam upāśnāti tair viruddhāny anātmavān
english: Not knowing his own constitution, his strength, and the season, the man without self-mastery eats unseasonably things harmful to them.

sanskrit: yadāyam atikaṣṭāni sarvāṇy upaniṣevate atyartham api vā bhuṅkte na vā bhuṅkte kadā cana
english: When he indulges in all manner of exceedingly harmful things, eats far too much, or at times eats not at all,

sanskrit: duṣṭānnaṃ viṣamānnaṃ ca so 'nyonyena virodhi ca guru vāpi samaṃ bhuṅkte nātijīrṇe 'pi vā punaḥ
english: and partakes of spoiled food, ill-balanced food, and food mutually incompatible, or heavy food along with too much, or again before what was eaten is digested,

sanskrit: vyāyāmam atimātraṃ vā vyavāyaṃ copasevate satataṃ karmalobhād vā prāptaṃ vegavidhāraṇam
english: or indulges in excessive exercise and in sexual intercourse, or out of greed for action constantly suppresses the natural urges as they arise,

sanskrit: rasātiyuktam annaṃ vā divāsvapnaṃ niṣevate apakvānāgate kāle svayaṃ doṣān prakopayan
english: or resorts to food too rich in flavors and to sleeping by day — while it is yet undigested, before the time has come — he himself stirs up the bodily humors,

sanskrit: svadoṣakopanād rogaṃ labhate maraṇāntikam atha codbandhanādīni parītāni vyavasyati
english: and from the inflaming of his own humors he contracts a disease that ends in death; or else, beset, he resolves upon hanging and the like.

sanskrit: tasya taiḥ kāraṇair jantoḥ śarīrāc cyavate yathā jīvitaṃ procyamānaṃ tad yathāvad upadhāraya
english: By such causes the life of that creature departs from the body — as I tell it, mark it well, just as it is.

sanskrit: ūṣmā prakupitaḥ kāye tīvravāyusamīritaḥ śarīram anuparyeti sarvān prāṇān ruṇaddhi vai
english: The bodily heat, inflamed and driven by a fierce wind, courses through the body and blocks all the vital airs.

sanskrit: atyarthaṃ balavān ūṣmā śarīre parikopitaḥ bhinatti jīvasthānāni tāni marmāṇi viddhi ca
english: That heat, grown exceedingly strong and inflamed within the body, splits open the seats of life — know these to be the vital points.

sanskrit: tataḥ savedanaḥ sadyo jīvaḥ pracyavate kṣaran śarīraṃ tyajate jantuś chidyamāneṣu marmasu vedanābhiḥ parītātmā tad viddhi dvijasattama
english: Then the life, full of anguish, at once flows out and departs; and the creature, its self beset by agonies as the vital points are riven, quits the body — know this, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: jātīmaraṇasaṃvignāḥ satataṃ sarvajantavaḥ dṛśyante saṃtyajantaś ca śarīrāṇi dvijarṣabha
english: Forever agitated by birth and death, all creatures are seen abandoning their bodies, O bull among the twice-born.

sanskrit: garbhasaṃkramaṇe cāpi marmaṇām atisarpaṇe tādṛśīm eva labhate vedanāṃ mānavaḥ punaḥ
english: And again, in the passage into the womb, when the vital points are pierced through, a man undergoes just such an agony once more.

sanskrit: bhinnasaṃdhir atha kledam adbhiḥ sa labhate naraḥ yathā pañcasu bhūteṣu saṃśritatvaṃ nigacchati śaityāt prakupitaḥ kāye tīvravāyusamīritaḥ
english: His joints loosened, that man then takes on moisture from the waters; thus, inflamed by cold within the body and driven by a fierce wind, he enters into union with the five elements.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa pañcasu bhūteṣu prāṇāpāne vyavasthitaḥ sa gacchaty ūrdhvago vāyuḥ kṛcchrān muktvā śarīriṇam
english: That breath which, amid the five elements, is established in the inward and outward airs — that upward-moving wind departs, releasing the embodied one with difficulty.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ ca jahāty eva nirucchvāsaś ca dṛśyate nirūṣmā sa nirucchvāso niḥśrīko gatacetanaḥ
english: It quits the body indeed, and breathless does the body appear: without warmth, without breath, without luster, its consciousness gone.

sanskrit: brahmaṇā saṃparityakto mṛta ity ucyate naraḥ srotobhir yair vijānāti indriyārthāñ śarīrabhṛt tair eva na vijānāti prāṇam āhārasaṃbhavam
english: Forsaken by Brahman, the man is called dead; by those channels through which the embodied one perceives the objects of the senses, by those very channels he no longer perceives the breath that arises from food.

sanskrit: tatraiva kurute kāye yaḥ sa jīvaḥ sanātanaḥ teṣāṃ yad yad bhaved yuktaṃ saṃnipāte kva cit kva cit tat tan marma vijānīhi śāstradṛṣṭaṃ hi tat tathā
english: That eternal life-principle which dwells in this very body — whatever among these humors is fittingly joined in confluence, here and there, know that to be a vital point, for so it is seen in the scriptures.

sanskrit: teṣu marmasu bhinneṣu tataḥ sa samudīrayan āviśya hṛdayaṃ jantoḥ sattvaṃ cāśu ruṇaddhi vai tataḥ sa cetano jantur nābhijānāti kiṃ cana
english: When those vital points are riven, it surges up, and entering the heart of the creature it swiftly blocks the inner sense; then the conscious creature can perceive nothing at all.

sanskrit: tamasā saṃvṛtajñānaḥ saṃvṛteṣv atha marmasu sa jīvo niradhiṣṭhānaś cāvyate mātariśvanā
english: His knowledge veiled by darkness, the vital points now closed over, that life-principle, left without a seat, is shaken loose by the wind.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa taṃ mahocchvāsaṃ bhṛśam ucchvasya dāruṇam niṣkrāman kampayaty āśu tac charīram acetanam
english: Then, drawing that great breath, exhaling fiercely and terribly, as it goes forth it swiftly sets that senseless body trembling.

sanskrit: sa jīvaḥ pracyutaḥ kāyāt karmabhiḥ svaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ aṅkitaḥ svaiḥ śubhaiḥ puṇyaiḥ pāpair vāpy upapadyate
english: That life-principle, fallen from the body, wrapped about by its own deeds, marked by its own meritorious good or by its evil, comes to a new birth.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā jñānasaṃpannā yathāvac chrutaniścayāḥ itaraṃ kṛtapuṇyaṃ vā taṃ vijānanti lakṣaṇaiḥ
english: Brāhmaṇas endowed with knowledge, whose certainties rest duly upon the sacred lore, recognize by signs the one who has done meritorious deeds and the other as well.

sanskrit: yathāndhakāre khadyotaṃ līyamānaṃ tatas tataḥ cakṣuṣmantaḥ prapaśyanti tathā taṃ jñānacakṣuṣaḥ
english: As those who have eyes behold a firefly flitting and merging this way and that in the darkness, so do those whose eye is knowledge behold it.

sanskrit: paśyanty evaṃvidhāḥ siddhā jīvaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā cyavantaṃ jāyamānaṃ ca yoniṃ cānupraveśitam
english: Perfected ones of such a kind behold with the divine eye the life-principle passing away, being born, and entering into a womb.

sanskrit: tasya sthānāni dṛṣṭāni trividhānīha śāstrataḥ karmabhūmir iyaṃ bhūmir yatra tiṣṭhanti jantavaḥ
english: Its abodes are seen here to be of three kinds, according to the scriptures: this earth is the field of action, where creatures abide.

sanskrit: tataḥ śubhāśubhaṃ kṛtvā labhante sarvadehinaḥ ihaivoccāvacān bhogān prāpnuvanti svakarmabhiḥ
english: Having done good and evil, all embodied beings then obtain — even here — high and low enjoyments, which they win by their own deeds.

sanskrit: ihaivāśubhakarmā tu karmabhir nirayaṃ gataḥ avāk sa niraye pāpo mānavaḥ pacyate bhṛśam tasmāt sudurlabho mokṣa ātmā rakṣyo bhṛśaṃ tataḥ
english: But here itself the man of evil deeds, gone to hell by his deeds, that sinful man is grievously cooked headlong in hell; therefore liberation is hard indeed to win, and the self must be guarded with the utmost care.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ tu jantavo gatvā yeṣu sthāneṣv avasthitāḥ kīrtyamānāni tānīha tattvataḥ saṃnibodha me tac chrutvā naiṣṭhikīṃ buddhiṃ budhyethāḥ karmaniścayāt
english: But the stations on high to which creatures go and where they abide — as they are recounted, learn them here from me in their truth; hearing that, you would attain a settled understanding through certainty about action.

sanskrit: tārārūpāṇi sarvāṇi yac caitac candramaṇḍalam yac ca vibhrājate loke svabhāsā sūryamaṇḍalam sthānāny etāni jānīhi narāṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām
english: All the forms of the stars, and this orb of the moon, and that orb of the sun which shines in the world by its own radiance — know these to be the abodes of men of meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: karmakṣayāc ca te sarve cyavante vai punaḥ punaḥ tatrāpi ca viśeṣo 'sti divi nīcoccamadhyamaḥ
english: And at the exhaustion of their deeds all of them fall away, again and again; and there too, in heaven, there is a distinction of low, high, and middling.

sanskrit: na tatrāpy asti saṃtoṣo dṛṣṭvā dīptatarāṃ śriyam ity etā gatayaḥ sarvāḥ pṛthaktve samudīritāḥ
english: Nor even there is there contentment, on beholding a yet more dazzling splendor. Thus all these destinies have been set forth in their separateness.

sanskrit: upapattiṃ tu garbhasya vakṣyāmy aham ataḥ param yathāvat tāṃ nigadataḥ śṛṇuṣvāvahito dvija
english: But the coming-to-be of the embryo I shall now declare hereafter; as I recount it duly, listen attentively, O twice-born one.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca śubhānām aśubhānāṃ ca neha nāśo 'sti karmaṇām prāpya prāpya tu pacyante kṣetraṃ kṣetraṃ tathā tathā
english: The brāhmaṇa said: For deeds, whether good or evil, there is no destruction here; meeting field upon field, in this way and that, they ripen.

sanskrit: yathā prasūyamānas tu phalī dadyāt phalaṃ bahu tathā syād vipulaṃ puṇyaṃ śuddhena manasā kṛtam
english: As a fruit-bearing tree, coming to fruition, yields fruit in plenty, so abundant is the merit that is wrought with a pure mind.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ cāpi tathaiva syāt pāpena manasā kṛtam purodhāya mano hīha karmaṇy ātmā pravartate
english: And sin too would be just the same, wrought with a sinful mind; for here, setting the mind in front, the self engages in action.

sanskrit: yathā karmasamādiṣṭaṃ kāmamanyusamāvṛtaḥ naro garbhaṃ praviśati tac cāpi śṛṇu cottaram
english: How, as ordained by his deeds, beset by desire and wrath, a man enters the womb — hear that too in what follows.

sanskrit: śukraṃ śoṇitasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ striyā garbhāśayaṃ gatam kṣetraṃ karmajam āpnoti śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
english: The seed, mingled with blood and entered into the womb of the woman, obtains a field born of its deeds, whether good or evil.

sanskrit: saukṣmyād avyaktabhāvāc ca na sa kva cana sajjate saṃprāpya brahmaṇaḥ kāyaṃ tasmāt tad brahma śāśvatam tad bījaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tena jīvanti jantavaḥ
english: By reason of its subtlety and unmanifest nature, it nowhere clings, having attained the body of Brahman; therefore that Brahman is eternal. It is the seed of all beings, and by it the creatures live.

sanskrit: sa jīvaḥ sarvagātrāṇi garbhasyāviśya bhāgaśaḥ dadhāti cetasā sadyaḥ prāṇasthāneṣv avasthitaḥ tataḥ spandayate 'ṅgāni sa garbhaś cetanānvitaḥ
english: That life-principle, entering all the limbs of the embryo part by part, at once sustains them by the mind, abiding in the seats of the vital airs; then the embryo, endowed with consciousness, sets its limbs astir.

sanskrit: yathā hi lohaniṣyando niṣikto bimbavigraham upaiti tadvaj jānīhi garbhe jīvapraveśanam
english: For as molten iron, poured out, takes on the form of the mold, even so understand the entering of the life-principle into the embryo.

sanskrit: lohapiṇḍaṃ yathā vahniḥ praviśaty abhitāpayan tathā tvam api jānīhi garbhe jīvopapādanam
english: As fire enters a ball of iron, heating it through, so too understand the coming-to-be of the life-principle within the embryo.

sanskrit: yathā ca dīpaḥ śaraṇaṃ dīpyamānaḥ prakāśayet evam eva śarīrāṇi prakāśayati cetanā
english: And as a blazing lamp lights up a dwelling, even so does consciousness light up the bodies.
